tasks.title: the three arms decide floor membership
tasks.acceptance: A unit is in the floor when it holds a digit, a backtick-delimited span, or one of §2.1's twelve listed verbs. The three arms are separately assertable. §11 rows 1 and 2 pass, row 2 on a bare `internal/cli/audit.go` carrying no digit.

tasks.title: text_sha and ordinal
tasks.acceptance: text_sha is the first twelve lowercase hex characters of the sha256 of the canonical unit text, UTF-8 encoded. ordinal is the 1-based index of a unit among those sharing its hash, in emission order. §11 row 18c passes on two units with identical canonical text.

tasks.title: --units prints every floor unit's full text
tasks.acceptance: One line per floor unit carrying unit_id, text_sha and the whole canonical text, never a truncation, with the hash equal to the sha256 of the text beside it. §11 row 4b passes.
source_sections: ### 2.2 The floor is a coverage obligation, not a shortlist

tasks.title: a pre-heading unit anchors to §0
tasks.acceptance: The anchor is the last §n(.n)* heading at or above the unit, and §0 before the first. A table row anchors to its own section, not to §0. §11 row 21 passes on this spec's preamble blockquote, and a table row in §7.2 reports §7.2.
source_sections: ### 7.3 Where it lives, and what it must not disturb

tasks.title: six verdicts, seven kinds, six tiers
tasks.acceptance: All six verdicts including NOT-A-CLAIM round-trip; kind and tier are closed enums; acceptability is a per-kind SET with no ordering anywhere in the implementation. §11 rows 5, 6 and 7 pass, row 6 asserting {document, run, PASS} and {behaviour, probe, PASS} both rejected.

tasks.title: the recorded row's field requirements
tasks.acceptance: §7.2's field table is a type with validation: unit_id nullable, anchor, text_sha, ordinal, verdict, kind and tier required except on NOT-A-CLAIM where they are optional, evidence required whenever tier is present, partial_kind iff PARTIAL, held_at iff partial_kind is true-when-written, causes iff QUESTION, carried_from optional. A row failing any cell is rejected naming the field.

tasks.title: the per-verdict acceptability rule at record
tasks.acceptance: PASS, PARTIAL and FAIL require an acceptable tier for the kind; QUESTION accepts either relation; UNVERIFIABLE carries a tier with no constraint. §11 row 7b passes with {behaviour, read, QUESTION} and {behaviour, run, QUESTION} both accepted.

tasks.title: a QUESTION carries three to five causes
tasks.acceptance: causes is an array of {cause, prediction} objects; lengths 2 and 6 are rejected, 3 and 5 accepted. §11 row 8 passes, and its mutant of a 1–10 bound fails it.
source_sections: ## 6. Ranked causes, facts, and not blocking

tasks.title: one invalid row writes no round file
tasks.acceptance: --record validates every row before writing; one invalid row means no round file and a state directory byte-identical to before the attempt. §11 row 10 passes.

tasks.title: ground artifacts are their own prefix list
tasks.acceptance: groundFilePrefixes holds ground-round-, snapshot-ground-round- and floor-ground-round-, and neither roundFilePrefixes nor snapshotPrefixes gains an entry. On a ground-only spec hasRecordedRoundFiles and hasStateArtifacts are both false and LoadReviewState returns (nil, nil) rather than a StateCorruptError. §11 row 11 passes.
source_sections: ### 7.3 Where it lives, and what it must not disturb
tasks.closed_reason:
- groundFilePrefixes holds ground-round-, snapshot-ground-round- and floor-ground-round- in internal/engine/reviewstate.go; roundFilePrefixes and snapshotPrefixes are byte-identical to HEAD, verified by diff
- TestGroundOnlyStateDirIsInvisibleToReviewState builds a ground-only directory in t.TempDir() and asserts hasRecordedRoundFiles and hasStateArtifacts both false and LoadReviewState returning (nil, nil) rather than a StateCorruptError, with require.NoFileExists on state.json so the fixture cannot pass by not being ground-only
- Section 11 row 11 passes: TestGroundArtifactsAreTheirOwnPrefixList asserts through hasAnyPrefixed on the three real artifact filenames rather than restating the prefixes, and was observed red four times before green, including row 11's named mutant of adding ground-round- to roundFilePrefixes

tasks.title: N is the highest ground round plus one
tasks.acceptance: A directory holding ground-round-1 and ground-round-3 yields N=4; a gap is preserved. §11 row 13 passes and its count-plus-one mutant fails.
source_sections: ### 7.3 Where it lives, and what it must not disturb

tasks.title: roundNumberRe gains ground
tasks.acceptance: roundNumberRe's alternation includes ground, so DeriveBookkeeping classifies a dirty ground-round-3.ndjson with ref "3" like its review and audit siblings rather than with the filename. Numbering still uses groundFilePrefixes.
source_sections: ### 7.3 Where it lives, and what it must not disturb

tasks.title: a ground round leaves state.json byte-identical
tasks.acceptance: Recording a ground round on a spec whose state.json already exists leaves that file byte-identical, and creates none on a spec without one. §11 rows 12 and 21b pass.
source_sections: ### 7.3 Where it lives, and what it must not disturb

tasks.title: tp ground emits its own isolation clause
tasks.acceptance: A third constant beside isolationClause and incrementalClause permits writing inside a copy the unit creates outside the repository and forbids every write inside it except the round's output file. A ground prompt ends with it and incrementalClause byte for byte, and that suffix differs from the one review and audit share. §11 row 18 passes; the assertion covers three commands over two suffixes.

tasks.title: tp ground emits prompt, snapshot, floor
tasks.acceptance: tp ground <spec> writes snapshot-ground-round-N.md and floor-ground-round-N.txt, creates spec/.tp-review/<base>/ when absent, and emits one prompt naming ground-rN.ndjson as its output_path. Editing the spec between emit and --record does not change the floor --record validates against. §11 rows 12 and 19 pass.
source_sections: ### 7.3 Where it lives, and what it must not disturb

tasks.title: tp ground --record validates against the recorded floor
tasks.acceptance: --record reads floor-ground-round-N.txt rather than re-deriving from the current spec, validates every row against §7.2, and writes ground-round-N.ndjson. --record with no prior emit exits 3 with a message naming the emit command.

tasks.title: each of 0/1/2/3/4 from a named input
tasks.acceptance: The mapping is taken from exitStateError: 1 for a row failing validation including a line that is not JSON, 2 for --check without --status and --record with no path, 3 for a missing --record file and a corrupt state directory, 4 for a held write lock. §11 row 14 passes with one test per code, and its mutant mapping a corrupt directory to 4 fails.

tasks.title: coverage is dispositions over the emitted floor
tasks.acceptance: Coverage counts dispositioned floor units over emitted floor units; a row with unit_id null moves neither side and appears in a separate count; UNVERIFIABLE counts as dispositioned. §11 row 15 passes and its mutant counting reader-added rows in the numerator fails.

tasks.title: the second pass carries on (text_sha, ordinal)
tasks.acceptance: A unit whose (text_sha, ordinal) matches the immediately preceding round carries its disposition into round N's own file with carried_from naming the source round; a unit changed by one character does not; a unit reverted to a wording last seen two rounds ago is uncovered. §11 row 16 passes over a three-round fixture, and row 18c over five identical units.

tasks.title: --status reports coverage and breakdown
tasks.acceptance: --status carries the ratio, the latest round's per-verdict counts and the NOT-A-CLAIM share, so a round of 84 FAILs and a round of 84 PASSes are distinguishable at identical coverage. §11 row 22 passes.

tasks.title: --status --check gates on coverage only
tasks.acceptance: --status --check exits 0 when coverage is complete and 1 otherwise, and gates nothing else. Non-Goal 3 holds: no tp command refuses on coverage.

tasks.title: tp review emits ungrounded once
tasks.acceptance: tp review carries an ungrounded object in the top-level envelope holding the latest ground round, the undispositioned count and the floor size, absent entirely when coverage is complete or no ground round exists, surviving --compact. Its exit code is identical with and without ungrounded units. §11 row 17 passes on a run emitting more than one role prompt.
source_sections: ## 9. Review is told, and not stopped

tasks.title: SKILL, REFERENCE and README carry tp ground
tasks.acceptance: skills/tp/SKILL.md gains the grounding workflow and its place before review; skills/tp/REFERENCE.md gains the row schema, the kind-tier sets, the exit codes and the ungrounded key; README.md gains the command. The pre-release checklist in CLAUDE.md is satisfied for all three.

tasks.title: what the derivation drops and how it blocks
tasks.acceptance: engine.FloorUnits takes the spec text, not a path. Fenced blocks, ATX headings, horizontal rules and table separator rows are dropped. What remains splits into blank-line-separated blocks, and each table data row is its own block.
tasks.closed_reason:
- engine.FloorUnits(text string) []string takes the spec's TEXT, not a path: internal/engine/floor.go opens no file, and TestFloorUnitsTakesTheSpecTextNotAPath writes a real file in t.TempDir, passes its path, and asserts the single returned unit is the path string. Observed red against a FloorUnits that os.ReadFile'd its argument (2 units, not 1). No test in the file reads spec/*.md.
- Fenced blocks, ATX headings, horizontal rules and table separator rows are dropped by floorBlocks, one table-driven case per class in TestFloorBlocksDropsWhatStep1Drops, each keeping prose on both sides. Observed red against five mutants, one per class: a fence arm setting inFence=false (content survives), a dropped heading arm, len(s)<2 as the rule length bound, a rule arm knowing only '-', and a separator row blocked as a data row. `-*-` and `--` are asserted NOT to be rules, so the bound and the same-marker rule are both pinned.
- What remains splits into blank-line-separated blocks (TestFloorBlocksSplitsOnBlankLines: whitespace-only line, runs of blanks, leading/trailing blanks, no-blank document, empty document). Observed red against a floorBlocks that never flushes on a blank line.
- Each table data row is its own block, carrying IsTableRow (TestEachTableDataRowIsItsOwnBlock, rows deliberately adjacent and bracketed by prose with no blank line). Observed red against a data row appended to the surrounding block. TestTableRowsInsideAFenceAreNotTableRows pins the rule order: a pipe line inside a fence is code.
- Ported from scripts/floor-prototype.py rather than designed: the blocking is byte-identical to the prototype's on seven real documents (1,248 blocks over spec/1.0.0.md, spec/0.1.0.md, spec/0.36.0.md, spec/0.37.0.md, CLAUDE.md, README.md, skills/tp/SKILL.md), checked with a throwaway test that was deleted afterwards. That comparison was itself shown to discriminate by mutating the horizontal-rule arm (16 blocks moved in spec/0.1.0.md, 2 in SKILL.md) — and the first two files I tried it on, spec/1.0.0.md and README.md, contain zero horizontal rules and reported MATCH under the mutant, so the check is only as strong as the constructs the file happens to hold.
- Steps 3 to 5 are left as a seam: floorUnitsFromBlock is the single place a block becomes units, so floor-tables and floor-canonical cannot make the prose and table paths diverge. The prototype's sentinel-string marker is replaced by a struct field, which removes the bug its own comment records (the sentinel matched no line in the file, so every table row anchored to §0).
- Quality gate green, all four steps: ./scripts/check-suite-state.sh (full suite, -race -count=1), golangci-lint run (0 issues), ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh, ./scripts/check-complexity.sh. deadcode passes with FloorUnits exported and only test-called because the script runs deadcode -test.

Out of scope: two observations on §2.1 that I implemented literally rather than resolving. (1) Step 1 says "drop" and step 2 says "split on blank lines", so a heading between two prose lines carrying no blank line leaves those lines in ONE block — the prototype does the same, and I pinned it in a test case ("a dropped line is dropped, not turned into a boundary"), but the spec never says so and a reader could conform either way. (2) §2.1 does not define "ATX heading" or "horizontal rule" precisely; the prototype's `^\s*#` also drops a line like `#tag`, and its rule test rejects markdown's legal spaced form (`- - -`). Both are ported verbatim so tp and the prototype agree, but a spec that named the patterns would remove the ambiguity.

tasks.title: a table data row becomes one unit
tasks.acceptance: A data row yields one unit with its cells joined by an em dash, however many full stops the cells hold. An escaped pipe is content, not a separator. Section 11 row 18d passes.

tasks.title: canonicalise, split and trim
tasks.acceptance: A leading blockquote prefix is stripped from every line, and a list marker only when the block first line opens a list. Lines join with one space, whitespace collapses, and prose splits at a terminator followed by whitespace with the terminator kept. Section 11 rows 18b and 20 pass, row 20 on a paragraph whose continuation line begins with an ordinal.

tasks.title: the emitted index rows
tasks.acceptance: Each floor unit emits unit_id, anchor, text_sha, ordinal and byte length, where unit_id is u followed by the index over every unit the derivation produces including cut ones. The index contains no substring of any unit text. Section 11 row 4 passes on a constructed 1200-unit floor.

tasks.title: cut rows, the commit line and the summary
tasks.acceptance: A cut unit emits its id and anchor with no hash and no text. The first line names the commit the index was derived from. The summary counts units rather than distinct hashes.
